title: DAOP: Data-Aware Offloading and Predictive Pre-Calculation for Efficient MoE Inference
problem: MoE models face deployment challenges on memory-constrained systems; GPU memory cannot hold all experts simultaneously, requiring frequent CPU-GPU data transfers that negate GPU speed advantages and degrade inference latency.
motivation: MoE effectiveness is limited by heterogeneous memory hierarchy; intelligent scheduling can reduce transfer overhead by exploiting activation patterns.
method: The system watches which experts each input sequence actually uses, then dynamically chooses whether each expert lives on the faster GPU or slower CPU storage. Before the GPU needs an expert, it predicts which one comes next and pre-calculates it on the CPU—so the answer is ready before the GPU requests it. This prediction-and-preparation strategy replaces the expensive CPU-GPU data transfers that normally happen. When GPU memory fills up, the system gracefully switches to using more CPU storage; it runs slower but stays accurate instead of crashing.
key_novelty: The system predicts which experts each input needs and pre-positions them to avoid the slow CPU-GPU data transfers that normally eliminate the GPU's speed advantage.
contributions: Per-sequence dynamic expert allocation between CPU and GPU
Predictive expert pre-calculation on CPU to overlap communication
Graceful degradation mechanism for flexible cache configurations
8.20x speedup over expert caching/prefetching, 1.35x over pure offloading
limitations: Evaluation on various datasets mentioned but specific dataset characteristics and MoE model sizes not detailed.
primary_theme: Intelligent CPU-GPU expert offloading for memory-efficient MoE inference
